biggest_gap.what: The round's headline measurements were taken in a world with nobody in it and no longer reproduce on the build that ships. machine.js:472 added a giver-presence term to open() — `giver absent: <npc> is not in this world`, gate 'giver_presence', with presenceMode defaulting to 'on' at machine.js:93 — after the round-2 numbers were taken. Neither faction-probe.mjs nor faction-seam-probe.mjs calls questPresenceGate, and both boot a bare world. Re-running the builder's own tool with its own command line takes the Wet Ledger from the 16/16 recorded on disk to 8/16: P3 7/18 quests offerable (was 18/18), P4 top derived rank 4 (was 7), P13 the seat is NOT vacated by play, P14 rank-7-and-non-violent FAIL, P15 17 questOpen calls refused, and P16 — the round's strongest claim — flips from 'the walk wrote no reputation at all; 398 was paid entirely by the quests' own consequences' to 'the walk WROTE reputation 10, 22, 36, 52, 70, 90, 112'. The cascade is causal: because open() refuses, faction-probe's grantRep() fallback fires to satisfy rank terms by hand, so the no-reputation-writes property was never independent of the gate.
biggest_gap.what_it_is_not: It is NOT that the faction content is unreachable. tools/quests/critic-giver-presence.mjs across every bootable state reports faction givers present 62/62 and talkable 62 — a better record than the mainline's 27/32. The content is placed; the instrument is not standing in the world.
biggest_gap.remedy: Make faction-probe.mjs and faction-seam-probe.mjs boot an inhabited state, or call questPresenceGate('report') and publish the miss list. Then re-run all three lines and EXPECT the report to change — a probe that returns 16/16 unchanged is still not standing in the world. Until then no reports/faction-probe-*.json figure may be cited, including every headline in orchestration/status/W1-FACTIONS-r2.json.

secondary_observations.what: Vocabulary drift silently disabled the build's only method/violence consistency guard on 43.7% of the round's new resolutions. Five new method values (comply, expose, lie, sabotage, investigate) are absent from RES_METHODS_NONVIOLENT. Broken on purpose with a passing control: the same defect goes RED on 'refuse' and GREEN on 'comply'. No resolution is currently mis-declared, so the harm today is entirely to the instrument — 'check-quests 120 quests PASS' is, for 38 of 87 resolutions, a pass the checker could not withhold.
secondary_observations.remedy: Make an UNRECOGNISED method a problem in its own right, rather than only adding the five values.

secondary_observations.what: The tic the prose sweep exists to catch got WORSE in material written after it was found. Journal register: ours 29.89 per 10k vs Morrowind's 0.00 across 3,183 reference entries. Splitting the faction lines, round-1 material runs 23.55/10k and round-2 material runs 30.90/10k — 1.31x. Raw: 22 instances / 12 quests (r1) vs 27 / 10 (r2). Q-ASSZ-12 uses 'eleven' NINE times, is titled 'Eleven Years of Not Asking', and contains the journal line 'she said the number eleven three times'. 'eleven years' appears 23 times across three unrelated fictions.
secondary_observations.remedy: 27 instances is an afternoon. Keep the Assize's eleven-year gap, which is load-bearing; re-roll the rest per line.

secondary_observations.what: Section D's fix is `questSetFlag(flag, false)` before the reading, but that CANNOT un-seed a topic — the probe's own comment says topics are permanent. The clean `before` reading is guaranteed by nothing except D having been moved to the top of the file. It fails SAFE (contamination goes red, not green), so it is a fragility rather than a false pass, and is not scored as one.
secondary_observations.remedy: A forgetTopic harness call, or a fresh world per case.

secondary_observations.what: The round-2 chooser ranks violence 100000, expels 50000, does-not-raise-a-ladder-flag 20000, unavailable 1000 — an optimiser pointed at the exact metric being reported. Reading the avoided set out of the live gate rather than hardcoding it is the right shape, and reporting it as expulsion_causes_avoided_by_the_walk is honest. But whether a TYPICAL character can walk the line remains untaken.

self_audit.self_audit_note: TWO OF MY OWN INSTRUMENTS WENT RED FOR THEIR OWN REASONS AND BOTH ARE REPORTED. (1) My first critic-faction-r2 run reported '0/17 givers, 53 of 53 quests given by nobody' and I was one paragraph from filing 'the faction content is unreachable' as the biggest gap; critic-giver-presence.mjs — a tool written by a different critic for a different piece — showed 62/62 faction givers present and talkable across the build's states, and the finding became a much narrower and more accurate one about the PROBE's boot condition. (2) My records_belief marker regex initially missed 'I do not think', reporting 4.2% where a corrected generous test reports 13.4%; only the corrected number is published. ran_every_assigned_method is false: the refusing walk and the multi-signature sweep stalled on my own chooser and are declared unmeasured rather than scored. I re-derived four builder numbers independently (18-per-line, 1005 journal entries, the 1.92x probe spread, the 5.33x declared spread) and DISAGREED with one (the reachable spread is 3.90x, not 5.33x and not 1.92x).

notes: Round 2 is a real round. GAP-FCT-01 is closed and the builder found a worse bug inside its own fix while closing it; both RI-QST01 hard fails are genuinely cleared and I re-derived them from the data without touching the builder's probe; the round-1 orphan factionLawFactor now has a world-side writer that I confirmed by my own perturbation with zero harness pokes. The score moves 4.1 -> 5.4. It does not reach the gate because two RI-CRM02 hard fails survive untouched, and because the artifacts that carry the round's best claims assert things the shipped build does not support and nothing in the tree says so.
